BENGALURU: The deaths of a 36-year-old man and his four-year-old son at their home in Chikkabanavara, Bengaluru, are being investigated as a double murder, with police arresting the man’s wife and her alleged boyfriend.Police identified the accused as A Harini, 26, and Vinay Kumar, a factory worker. The two, who became friends through social media about two years ago, have been remanded in police custody for five days for questioning.Police said Harini called the police control room around 7am on Monday, claiming that her husband Abhinandan and their son Yaduveer were lying motionless inside their residence in Guddebasaveshwara.When police reached the house, they noticed several inconsistencies.CCTV cameras inside and outside the house had been switched off around 10pm on Sunday. There were also no signs of forced entry. Investigators found that call logs and messages had been deleted from Harini’s phone.Police said Harini initially gave contradictory answers during questioning before allegedly admitting to the crime.According to police, Harini allegedly let Vinay into the house around 11pm.He had been waiting outside for her signal and switched off his mobile phone before entering.Abhinandan was in the bathroom when the attack began. Police said the duo assaulted him and repeatedly dashed his head against the wall before Vinay allegedly choked him.The commotion woke Yaduveer, who came towards the bathroom and saw his father being attacked. The child screamed on witnessing the assault.Harini allegedly took Yaduveer into the bedroom and threatened him, telling him to go back to sleep.Vinay then allegedly dragged Abhinandan’s body into the bedroom, where the two placed it on the bed.Police said the duo then decided to kill Yaduveer because he had witnessed the attack.Harini and Vinay have given conflicting accounts of the child’s death. While Harini is said to have claimed that Vinay smothered the boy, Vinay accused Harini of killing him.DCP (northwest division) Nagesh DL said the accused had initially planned to eliminate Abhinandan. However, the situation took a darker turn when the child witnessed the attack.Police suspect the alleged motive was both personal and financial. Preliminary inquiry suggests that Harini and Vinay believed Abhinandan’s death would leave Harini as the owner of his property, including the family home and three acres of land in Kunigal.Family members told police that Harini and Abhinandan had a troubled marriage.A relative said Harini left the house in January following frequent disputes but returned after senior family members intervened.Another family member recalled that she left home again around four months ago, leaving behind a note saying she wanted to start a new life.Relatives later persuaded her to return and continue her marriage with Abhinandan.Police also recovered a cloth allegedly used to clean blood from the bathroom.Cops said Abhinandan’s head injuries had caused considerable bleeding. The accused allegedly cleaned the bathroom and his head before washing the cloth and leaving it to dry in the backyard.Vinay switched phone back on after reaching homePolice said Vinay kept his phone switched off while carrying out the crime.After leaving the house, he travelled to his home in Harohalli near Kanakapura and switched the phone back on only after reaching there.Police arrested him from his residence in the early hours of Tuesday.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as A Harini, 26, and Vinay Kumar, a factory worker. The two, who became friends through social media about two years ago, have been remanded in police custody for five days for questioning. Harini called the police control room around 7am on Monday claiming that her husband Abhinandan and their son Yaduveer were lying motionless inside their residence in Guddebasaveshwara.

Article Title: ‘All trade, commercial exchanges halted’: How UAE responded to Iran’s latest ballistic missile attack
Article Text:
A view of the Dubai city skyline. (AP Photo)

UAE freezes economic ties with Tehran

Iran denies launching missiles

Missile attack threatens fragile UAE-Iran thaw

Strait of Hormuz tensions add to pressure

Trump tensions with Oman over Iran deal

Iran says Strait will not reopen yet

The United Arab Emirates has suspended all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran after accusing Tehran of launching two ballistic missiles towards the Gulf state, dealing a fresh blow to efforts to ease tensions between the two countries.The UAE defence ministry said its air-defence systems detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards its territory on Tuesday. The incident triggered an emergency alert on residents' phones and was described as the first direct Iranian attack on the UAE since May.The ministry later said its assessment indicated that the missiles had been targeting maritime traffic. One missile fell into the sea outside the UAE's territorial waters, while the other fell within them. No damage or injuries were reported.Following the missile incident, the UAE foreign affairs ministry announced that it was halting economic engagement with Iran until further notice.The ministry said that “in light of regional escalations that undermine regional and international peace and security, all trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran have been halted until further notice”.The decision threatens to reverse a gradual restoration of economic and diplomatic links between Abu Dhabi and Tehran. Trade between the UAE and Iranian ports had resumed in some areas, while certain Iranian flights to the UAE had also quietly returned.The emergency alert issued on Tuesday was the first such warning in several months, apart from a false alert in June. Dubai's financial district had also begun filling up with bankers, while Emirati authorities had started allowing some 20,000 Iranian residents who were outside the country when the war began to return to the UAE.Iran has denied the UAE's accusation, with Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejecting the claim and warning that such allegations could undermine regional efforts to rebuild trust.Baghaei “completely rejected” the UAE's claim and expressed regret over the accusations against Iran, according to a statement issued by the Iranian Foreign Ministry.“This behaviour is contrary to the principle of good neighbourliness and disrupts ongoing efforts to strengthen trust between regional countries and prevent the escalation of insecurity in the region,” Baghaei said.The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson also called on regional countries to refrain from making “baseless accusations” against Tehran.“The Foreign Ministry spokesman called on all regional parties to refrain from making baseless accusations against the Islamic Republic of Iran, considering the existing complexities due to the ongoing evils of the US and the Zionist regime against regional peace and security, especially the history of numerous false flag operations,” he said.The UAE defence ministry, meanwhile, maintained that its air-defence systems had detected the missiles.“The first fell outside the country's territorial waters, while the second fell within its territorial waters,” the UAE Ministry of Defence said in a post on X.The UAE military said its forces remained on high alert and were prepared to respond to threats against the country's security and sovereignty.The latest confrontation comes after more than two months of efforts by Abu Dhabi and Tehran to reduce tensions that had escalated following the US and Israeli war against Iran that began on February 28.During the conflict, Iran launched repeated missile and drone attacks against neighbouring Gulf states, including the UAE, accusing them of enabling US and Israeli military operations.The UAE was among the Gulf states most heavily targeted, sustaining almost 3,000 missile and drone attacks. Abu Dhabi also carried out scores of strikes against Iran, taking a more hawkish position towards Tehran than several of its Gulf neighbours.Tensions later eased after Washington and Tehran reached a memorandum of understanding in June. However, the agreement began to unravel in early July, after which Iran shifted much of its military focus towards Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.In recent months, the UAE had sought to rebuild diplomatic and economic channels with Iran while maintaining close military ties with Israel and the United States. Emirati officials have repeatedly said they want to avoid being drawn further into a wider regional conflict.That balancing act is now under growing pressure following the latest missile incident.The confrontation also comes amid escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global oil and natural gas shipments.The UAE accused Iran earlier this month of attacking ships operated by Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the strategic waterway. Tehran has also maintained restrictions on traffic through the strait while issuing increasingly aggressive military rhetoric.A separate maritime incident was reported on Tuesday when an unidentified projectile struck a ship as it sailed out of the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre said the strike damaged the vessel's engine room and caused a casualty, while the Omani Coast Guard assisted other crew members.Another cargo vessel was struck by multiple projectiles about 40 nautical miles, or 74 kilometres, southeast of Mokha in Yemen and was declared a “constructive total loss”, according to the British maritime monitoring agency. The agency did not identify the projectiles or those responsible.The incidents have added to concerns over the safety of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Red Sea region, both vital routes for global trade.The maritime crisis has also drawn Oman into a dispute between Washington and Tehran over arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.US President Donald Trump threatened Oman after becoming dissatisfied with an emerging agreement between Muscat and Tehran aimed at managing ship traffic through the strategic waterway, according to two regional officials cited by The Associated Press.The officials said the Trump administration objected to parts of the proposed agreement, including joint Iranian and Omani management of the exit route from the strait and voluntary fees on vessels linked to security and maritime environmental protection.Trump on Monday threatened to bomb Oman as it worked with Iran on an agreement intended to reopen the strait and potentially allow Washington and Tehran to resume negotiations aimed at ending the conflict.He later posted a map on social media depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory. Trump had previously floated the idea during an Oval Office exchange, saying, “I like the idea of declaring it a territory,” without providing further details.The White House referred to Trump's earlier Oval Office remarks when asked about the latest comments and declined to provide additional details.Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded to Trump's remarks on social media.“Just as Trump correctly wrote the name of the eternal Persian Gulf, his delusion regarding the Strait of Hormuz will soon either be corrected, or we will correct this deluded man’s delusions for him,” Gharibabadi wrote on X.Trump has previously threatened Oman over its dealings with Iran. In May, he told reporters during a Cabinet meeting that Oman “will behave just like everybody else, or we will have to blow them up.”Iran has maintained that the Strait of Hormuz will not fully reopen until Washington meets its conditions, including commitments related to sanctions, frozen assets and military operations.“Until the United States fulfills its commitments under the agreement, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions, ending threats and military operations on all fronts, and implementing the other conditions to which it committed, the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen,” Iranian parliamentary speaker and former US-Iran negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said.Trump, however, said on Tuesday that the United States had no planned talks with Iran and insisted that the strait was “open and operating”, despite limited maritime traffic and reports of fresh attacks.He also said the US blockade of the waterway remained “in full force and effect” and claimed that all water mines had been removed.Egypt has backed the Iranian-Omani negotiations, saying an agreement could help create conditions for Washington and Tehran to return to talks.The Egyptian foreign ministry said the agreement could pave the way for a “comprehensive and permanent deal that addresses all concerns and enhances regional security and stability."The latest developments leave the UAE facing renewed security pressure as its decision to suspend economic ties with Iran threatens to derail a fragile diplomatic thaw, while tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and wider regional military activity continue to intensify.
Article Summary: The United Arab Emirates has suspended all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran. The UAE has accused Tehran of launching two ballistic missiles towards the Gulf state. The incident triggered an emergency alert on residents' phones and was described as the first direct Iranian attack on the UAE since May. Iran has denied the UAE's accusation.

Article Title: At least 9 killed, 6 injured in massive fire at hotel in Kolkata
Article Text:
The deceased were Bangladeshi citizens who had travelled to Kolkata for medical treatment.

8 killed in separate incident





KOLKATA: At least nine people were killed and six others injured after a massive fire broke out at a hotel in Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street early on Wednesday, officials said.According to news agency ANI, the deceased were Bangladeshi citizens who had travelled to Kolkata for medical treatment.The fire broke out at around 2am.Fire department personnel reached the spot and launched a rescue operation.According to a senior official, 80 people have been rescued from the five-storey building.Six people were injured in the incident and were taken for treatment. Officials said further details about the cause of the fire and the circumstances surrounding the deaths were being investigated."The dense smoke made it difficult for firefighters to climb the staircase and reach the upper floors. While nine people have died, more deaths are feared," a police officer told PTI."Our priority is to rescue those trapped and determine the reasons for the fire. The flames have been doused, and the cooling process is underway," he added.West Bengal Fire Department headquarters is located close to the hotel building.Speaking to PTI, Fire department minister Kaushik Chowdhury, "The situation inside this building is very bad.There are several hotels inside this building. I am shocked to see what was going on here."Asked about the cause of the fire, the minister said that it could be because of a short circuit. "But a forensic examination would reveal what led to the blaze," he said."The building management did not comply with basic safety and construction norms. It is alleged that there were several irregularities in the functioning of the hotel," the minister added.In a separate incident in Birbhum district, at least eight people were killed after fire broke out at a private hotel in Tarapith on Tuesday.The fire broke out at around 5am on the ground floor of the four-storey Hotel Bideshinii, located near a pond and a short distance from Tarapith police station.Most of the guests were asleep when the blaze began.Firefighters reached the hotel and brought the fire under control. The injured were rescued and taken to Rampurhat Government Medical College and Hospital for treatment.
Article Summary: A massive fire broke out at a hotel in Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street early on Wednesday. 80 people have been rescued from the five-storey building. Six people were injured in the incident and were taken for treatment. In a separate incident in Birbhum district, at least eight people were killed.

Article Title: 'Ready to deal with any threats': UAE vows response after Iran fires two missiles
Article Text:
The missile launches came as efforts continued to reach an agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

The United Arab Emirates’ defence ministry said on Tuesday that it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards the Gulf country, as tensions continued to rise across the region.The ministry said both missiles fell into water, with one landing outside the UAE’s territorial waters and the other inside them. It said the country remained prepared to respond to any threats.“The Ministry of Defence confirms that it is on high alert and fully prepared to deal with any threats, and to firmly confront anything aimed at undermining the security of the state, thereby ensuring the preservation of its sovereignty, security and stability, and protecting its interests and national capabilities,” it added.The ministry said that it is 'ready to deal with any threats.'The missile launches came as efforts continued to reach an agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global shipping. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the US had no talks planned with Iran, while insisting the strait remained “open and operating” despite sharply reduced traffic.Trump also said the US blockade of Iranian ports remained “in full force and effect” and claimed that all water mines had been removed.He posted a map depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory.Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded on X, saying: “Just as Trump correctly wrote the name of the eternal Persian Gulf, soon his delusion regarding the Strait of Hormuz will either be corrected or we will correct the delusions of this deluded man," he wrote on X.Shipping data platform Kpler said confirmed crossings through the Strait of Hormuz fell 19.5% last week to 95, with only three vessels passing through on Sunday. No vessels used the Omani routes.Meanwhile, an unidentified projectile damaged the engine room of a ship near Oman, causing “a crew casualty”, according to the British military’s UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. The Omani Coast Guard was assisting the crew, while authorities investigated.Separately, Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed they had launched drones at an oil refinery operated by Saudi Aramco in Saudi Arabia. There were no immediate reports of damage.
Article Summary: The United Arab Emirates’ defence ministry said on Tuesday that it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran. The ministry said both missiles fell into water, with one landing outside the UAE’s territorial waters and the other inside them. It said the country remained prepared to respond to any threats.

Article Title: Trump’s new election guru? India
Article Text:
Trump cited remarks by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar questioning how Americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification (Photo: Reuters)

TOI correspondent from Washington:

United States President Donald Trump has apparently discovered the solution to America’s notoriously fickle and complicated election system: Ask India.In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump cited purported remarks by India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar questioning how Americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification. Trump noted that about 646 million Indians voted in the last general election, with less than 1 per cent voting by mail, and every voter was required to have valid identification to argue: “We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!” US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor promptly agreed with Trump in a follow-up post.The hotly-contested Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, or SAVE Act, would require documentary proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections and establish national photo-ID requirements. It has passed the Republican-controlled House of Representatives but repeatedly stalled in the Senate, where Republicans lack the 60 votes to overcome the filibuster. Even some Republicans have baulked at pushing it through without broader support.MAGA principals say the measure is simple: only citizens should vote, and the government should verify that they are citizens. Democrats and voting-rights groups counter that federal law already prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections, documented cases of noncitizen voting are exceedingly rare, and MAGA fear-mongering that millions of non-citizens are voting have been repeatedly disproven.That has produced an inevitable political fracas: critics believe the law's practical effect would be to disproportionally disenfranchise poor, minority, elderly and other voters – which they say is the MAGA game plan – because these groups tend to vote Democratic.So while Republicans call that accusation partisan scaremongering, opponents call it voter suppression dressed up as election security. They argue that the bill creates paperwork barriers for legitimate voters who may lack passports, birth certificates or other acceptable documents, or whose names differ between documents.According to the Brennan Center for Justice, a non-partisan policy institute, more than 21 million voting-age Americans do not have ready access to a passport, birth certificate or naturalization papers. Millions more possess citizenship documents whose names may not match their current legal names. Married women who changed their surnames are one obvious example.Even otherwise, the legislation has become much more than a debate about an ID card; It is also a debate about who should run American elections. And this where Trump's India analogy gets interesting.India has a centralized Election Commission of India which administers national parliamentary and state-assembly elections with standardized procedures and voter identification. America deliberately went in the opposite direction. The Founding Fathers were suspicious of concentrating political power in the federal government, so the US Constitution left substantial responsibility for conducting elections with the states, while giving Congress power to regulate federal elections.So while Congress has enacted national election laws, including voter-registration and election-administration requirements, the day-to-day machinery remains overwhelmingly decentralized. Thus America ended up with thousands of election jurisdictions, varying registration procedures, differing ID requirements, different early- and mail-voting rules.And this constitutional architecture was designed when there were 13 states, not 50, and when the word “instantaneous” would have been considered an ambitious description of horse drawn carriages which plowed through snow in winter to ferry ballot boxes and officials (which is why US elections takes place on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November, but a new President takes oath almost ten weeks later on January 20 after a laborious process).The US system has plenty of weaknesses: registration errors, voter-roll disputes, gerrymandering, unequal procedures, campaign-finance problems, partisan election administration and endless arguments over mail ballots and voting machines. India's system isn't perfect either. Its elections face controversies over money and political influence, voter rolls, and persistent disputes over electronic voting machines.So while neither country has perfect elections, Trump appears to have concluded that America's complicated old electoral jalopy needs an Indian owner's manual, which itself is far from perfect.
Article Summary: Trump cited purported remarks by India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar questioning how Americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification. Trump noted that about 646 million Indians voted in the last general election, with less than 1 per cent voting by mail, and every voter was required to have valid identification.

Article Title: ‘When there are roads, accidents happen’: Pune MLA’s remark after 11-year-old’s death triggers row
Article Text:
Local MLA Shankar Mandekar (L; Photo credit: Facebook/@Shankar Mandekar) stated accidents happen when roads exist, drawing anger





PUNE: While the opposition blamed state government’s inaction for the pothole-ridden roads that claimed the life of an 11-year-old boy in Pune’s Mahalunge area on Monday, the local MLA from NCP, Shankar Mandekar, made a controversial statement in which he said that since there are roads, accidents happen.Mandekar visited the accident spot on Monday afternoon where, during the media interaction, he made the controversial remarks.“It was an unfortunate incident but when there are roads, accidents do happen. In the end, the case is registered against the owner of the bigger vehicle involved in the accident,” the Bhor MLA said.Local residents expressed anger over the poor road conditions and said that despite repeated complaints, the road was not repaired by the authorities.When Mandekar was asked about the delay in improving the road condition, he said, “I have been raising the issue in the assembly but beyond that what can I do? Even though I am a member of the party which is in the govt, the decision is taken by the concerned ministers.”The opposition parties have slammed the state government over the poor road conditions that claimed the life of the boy on Monday.NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said, “The chief minister chaired a meeting on July 10, 2025, to address the issues of Rajiv Gandhi Infotech park, Hinjewadi and Maan-Mahalunge. In that meeting, it was decided that single point authority will resolve all the issues. However, it has been more than a year; no progress has been made after that meeting. Now when an 11-year-old boy died in front of his father’s eyes, who should be held responsible for it?”Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray, who visited the area on Tuesday, said, “The local residents had held a protest at the same location demanding administration to repair the roads but the administration did not respond. Now after the death of the boy, govt will give compensation of Rs 4-5 lakh to the family but that does not solve the issue.”
Article Summary: An 11-year-old boy was killed in a road accident in Pune's Mahalunge area on Monday. Shankar Mandekar, local MLA from NCP, made a controversial statement in which he said that since there are roads, accidents happen. Local residents expressed anger over the poor road conditions.

Article Title: Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
Article Text:
Police registered an FIR after a woman sub-inspector alleged that the BJP MLA's daughter tried to bypass the queue and assaulted her. (Photo: Instagram)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The daughter of Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda was booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector following an argument at a temple in Mandya district in Karnataka, police said on Friday.The incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations, news agency PTI reported.According to the complaint filed by the woman police officer, she was deployed at the temple for security duty when Aishwarya , the MLA's daughter, allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.The police officer alleged that she asked Aishwarya to wait to avoid inconvenience to other devotees. According to the complaint, Aishwarya then identified herself as the daughter of an MLA and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing the officer and hitting her on the head. The complainant also alleged that she was threatened and prevented from performing her official duties.Based on the complaint, the Kyathanahalli police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation, a senior police officer said.However, the case has taken another turn, with Aishwarya filing a counter-complaint against the police officer.Police said an inquiry into her allegations has been initiated, but no FIR has been registered on the basis of her complaint so far. Further action will depend on the findings of the inquiry.Speaking to reporters, Tumakuru Rural MLA B Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct and said that anyone found guilty should face legal consequences."If she has committed a mistake, it is wrong. Whoever has done the mistake should face the consequences under the law," he said.The BJP legislator said his daughter had visited the temple with her two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly because waiting in the queue could have caused inconvenience.He also claimed that another person had been allowed to enter ahead of her, prompting his daughter to question the decision.While acknowledging that the argument had escalated, Gowda said his daughter should have shown greater restraint, particularly because she comes from a political family."I apologise on behalf of my daughter if she has made a mistake," he said.The MLA also called for a departmental inquiry into the incident and urged authorities to take action against anyone found responsible.
Article Summary: Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda's daughter booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector. Incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations. Aishwarya Gowda allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:
All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.​

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy. The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres. Campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.

Article Title: Zeeshan Siddique gets death threat from Portugal number, caller claims Godara gang link
Article Text:
NCP leader Zeeshan Siddique reported receiving a death threat from a Portugal-based number (File photo)





MUMBAI: National Congress Party leader and MLC Zeeshan Siddique filed a complaint soon after he arrived in Mumbai on Friday morning after a fresh threat he received while he was in London at 2.36 (which was 7.06 am IST).Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person based on an audio threat he received on August 12.Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal number.Siddique confirmed TOI that Bandra police registered an NC based on the complaint he submitted."The audio threat that lasted 1.29 minutes was received on my WhatsApp number by the same person who identified himself as Zeeshan Akhtar. My sister filed the first NC on August 6 while I was abroad. Now, the death threat audio clip was sent directly to me using Portugal number. In November 2025, we filed the writ and soon my security cover was reduced from eight cops to two. Also, there was 22 cops deployed at my residence which was reduced to zero," he said.The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint and threatened he will the one to kill him.TOI extracts the transcript of the threat audio which states, "Listen here, Zeeshan Siddique, this is Zeeshan Akhtar speaking. Listen to me carefully: I am going to kill you. Before I even touch your father... well, I had already assigned a team to the task two years ago, back when I was in police custody, got it?""Brother, everyone I’ve killed, I did so openly. Now, your end has come. Don't push your sister to the forefront; if you have the guts, go file the complaint yourself. I know everything; I’m aware of every detail. You might not die today or tomorrow, but within a year, you will definitely die. I have no problem with your money and I am not threatening you for money. The person claimed that he object to my illegal business and for which he will kill me.
